title: Introduce adaptive onboarding sampler and deterministic changelog compactor
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: onboarding new model variants currently produces noisy changelogs and large release notes because sampling is workload-agnostic and random seeds vary across runs. This PR adds an adaptive, budget-aware onboarding sampler plus a deterministic changelog compactor that groups sample deltas into coherent micro-changes. Goals: 1) reduce churn in release notes for small perf/noise deltas, 2) ensure sampled probes are representative of declared workload tiers, 3) produce deterministic, small-size changelog fragments suitable for auto-release briefs. High level design: the sampler uses workload tags from manifest (production|latency-sensitive|cost-sensitive) to weight probe selection and enforces a configurable token/compute budget per intake; a deterministic seeding layer hashes model metadata+manifest+run-id to produce repeatable sample seeds across CI and on-demand replays; the compactor applies delta-clustering heuristics on evaluation traces (latency, p50/p95, token-efficiency, quality score) to collapse semantically-equivalent minor changes into a single micro-entry and attach a confidence score. Backwards compatibility: sampler falls back to legacy uniform sampling when workload tags absent; changelog compactor annotates rather than removes context so manual reviewers can expand entries. Checklist: - [x] sampler algorithm and config (sampling_policy.rs, sampler.py) - [x] deterministic seed function and cross-language tests - [x] compactor logic and summarizer - [x] unit tests for sampler and compactor - [x] integration test with onboarding pipeline (CI job onboard-e2e) - [x] docs update in docs/onboarding/README.md - [x] Linear tickets linked. Impact: reduces typical generated changelog size by ~45% in internal benchmark and reduces noisy rerolls observed in automated rollouts. Rollout plan: feature-flagged via ONBOARD_ADAPTIVE_SAMPLER and gradual enable in staging->canary->main. See release_notes for customer-facing blurb.
commits_summary: feat(sampler): add workload-conditioned sampler and budget enforcement | feat(seed): deterministic seed derivation from manifest+run | feat(compactor): add delta-clustering and micro-entry serializer | test: add unit/integration tests and golden fixtures | docs: onboarding sampler usage and config examples | ci: add onboard-e2e pipeline job
review_comments: Ethan Zhao: Suggest making the default token budget conservative (suggest 10k tokens) and add a safety cap; Author reply: lowered default to 8k and added MAX_BUDGET env var with tests.

Rhea Gupta: Can the deterministic seed include toolchain hash to avoid cross-language drift?; Author reply: included a toolchain_version field in the seed input and added cross-language golden seeds in tests.

Oliver Kim: Compactor heuristics look good but we should surface the clustered metric breakdown to the console; Author reply: added per-cluster metrics (count, mean delta, confidence) to observability and example dashboard snippet in docs.
ci_checks: onboard-unit-tests: pass | compactor-unit-tests: pass | sampler-integration: pass | lint: pass | onboard-e2e: pass
performance_notes: Internal benchmark on 50 candidate variants: mean changelog size reduced 45% (median 48%); false-collapse rate estimated 1.8% on heldout evaluation; sampling budget reduced compute cost by ~22% for small-intake jobs.
release_notes: Feature: Adaptive onboarding sampler and deterministic changelog compactor. Summary: Onboarded models will produce smaller, more stable changelogs and more representative probe sets by default. Rolling out behind feature flag. Migration: none required. Notes: to opt-out set ONBOARD_ADAPTIVE_SAMPLER=false.
notes: This PR was driven by ENG-4123 intake stability task after multiple onboarding rerolls during the March benchmarking window. Canaries showed stable rollouts with feature enabled.
